# Ibis of Wound Products (`ibis-of-wound-products`)

Checks skin substitute and wound product billing: products billed with no purchase invoice, units over the product opened, JW and JZ waste modifiers against the waste recorded, application codes against the wound area, and products paid below what they cost. Patient names are masked before results reach the model.

**Ibis never submits or changes claims. Ibis never orders or pays for products.**

Kestrel ver 1 · Specialty billing · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · patient and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`kestrel-core`](../kestrel-core)

```bash
npx -y ibis-of-wound-products demo
npx -y ibis-of-wound-products mcp --root ./practice-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional data only: a made-up wound clinic, made-up patients, products priced for the example. Any likeness to real people or prices is chance.

- [`claims.csv`](fixtures/claims.csv), [`product-usage.csv`](fixtures/product-usage.csv) and [`invoices.csv`](fixtures/invoices.csv). Planted:
  - W1: 16 sq cm opened and 12 applied, but all 16 units billed on one line with JZ (no waste) instead of 12 plus 4 with JW.
  - W2: 30 units billed from a 25 sq cm product.
  - W3: a 49 sq cm wound billed with 15271 only; the area supports 15271 plus one unit of 15272.
  - W4: lot L-777 has no purchase invoice.
  - W5: billed correctly (12 applied, 4 with JW) but paid 900 for a product that cost 1200.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `ibis_check` | List products with no invoice, unit and waste modifier problems, application code mismatches and products paid below cost. | runs |
| `ibis_write_report` | Write ibis-wound-products.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and ibis-wound-products.html into out_dir (default kestrel-out/ibis). | runs |
| `ibis_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `ibis_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `ibis_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `ibis_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `claim_submit` | Ibis never submits or changes claims. | refused |
| `product_order` | Ibis never orders or pays for products. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `ibis_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `claims` (required) | Claim lines under --root: patient, date, code, modifiers, units, paid |
| `usage` (required) | Product usage log: patient, date, product code, lot, sq cm opened, sq cm applied, wound area |
| `invoices` (required) | Product invoices: product code, lot, invoice number, size in sq cm, cost |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold patient or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx ibis-of-wound-products inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Claim lines (`claims`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `patient_id` | text (masked) | Patient ID, Patient #, Patient Number, MRN, Medical Record Number, Chart #, Chart Number, Account # |
| `patient_name` | text (masked) | Patient, Patient Name, Name, Client, Client Name, Member, Member Name, Beneficiary |
| `date` (required) | date | Date of Service, DOS, Service Date, Visit Date, Date, From DOS, Session Date, Appointment Date |
| `cpt` (required) | text | CPT, Code, Procedure, Procedure Code, CPT/HCPCS, HCPCS, Service Code, Proc Code |
| `modifiers` | text | Modifiers, Modifier, Mod, Mods, Modifier 1, Mod 1 |
| `units` | number | Units, Unit, Qty, Quantity, Days/Units, Service Units |
| `paid` | amount | Paid, Paid Amount, Payment, Insurance Paid, Amount Paid, Allowed Paid |

### Product usage (`usage`)

| Column | Type | Read from |

### Invoices (`invoices`)

| Column | Type | Read from |

| `invoice` | text | Invoice, Invoice #, Invoice Number, PO, PO # |

## Memory

`ibis_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `ibis_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `kestrel-core` and `remedy-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ibis-of-wound-products": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "ibis-of-wound-products",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/practice-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add ibis-of-wound-products -- npx -y ibis-of-wound-products mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
ibis-of-wound-products tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
ibis-of-wound-products sources               # the columns each input is read from
ibis-of-wound-products inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
ibis-of-wound-products call ibis_check '{"claims":"<claims>","usage":"<usage>","invoices":"<invoices>"}'
ibis-of-wound-products eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
ibis-of-wound-products demo
```

## Patient and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: patient and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to an EHR, practice-management system, payer portal, clearinghouse, state system, HR or payroll system, or bank.
- Payer, Medicare, Medicaid, state and federal rules are summarised from public material as of 2026, and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, compliance or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, billing, coding, tax, clinical or HIPAA advice. It does not diagnose or recommend care. A person decides what to bill, pay, report, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
